=== enroll
$ orion-agent enroll --core-url https://core.example.com

 ┃ One-time token
 ┃ › ••••••••••••••••••••••••
 ┃ From Servers › Add server. Works once.

   ✓ Reachable
   ✓ Token accepted
   ✓ Enrolled as edge-05

   ▸ orion-agent service start

=== token apply
$ orion-agent token apply

 ┃ Replacement token
 ┃ › ••••••••••••••••••••••••••••••••••••••••
 ┃ 64 characters, from the Console. Your identity and monitors are kept.

   ✓ Token saved
   ✓ Identity preserved agt_3f9c1a · 5 monitors

   ▸ orion-agent service restart

=== reconfigure and state init
$ orion-agent reconfigure

   ✓ Service stopped
   ✓ Registration reset
   ✓ Registered again 5 monitors
   ✓ Service started

$ orion-agent state init

   ✓ State database ready /var/lib/orion/state.db

--- notes
NOTE Secrets never echo: Token inputs are masked (Huh password mode). Flags and files still work for automation, with --token-file recommended.
NOTE Two different tokens: The one-time orn_enr_ token adds a server. The 64-character replacement token is only for token apply. Each prompt says which.
NOTE Short and idempotent: Re-running on an enrolled host says so and does nothing.
